diffs.diff: header pin 1: part says D, datasheet reading says -
diffs.evidence: Same three signals, opposite listing order: the DFRobot 'Digital Push Button' schematic (Revision V2) labels the connector 'GND J1 3 2 1', with GND tied to J1 pin 3, the KEY/VCC net on pin 2 and the R1 1K output (D) on pin 1, so pin 1 is D as the model says; the second reading copied the V3 board's silkscreen top-to-bottom ('-', '+', 'D'), which runs from pin 3 to pin 1.

diffs.diff: header pin 3: part says GND, datasheet reading says D
diffs.evidence: The DFRobot schematic draws the ground symbol directly on J1 pin 3 (text 'GND J1 3 2 1'), and the output through R1 1K on pin 1, so pin 3 is GND (black wire) as the model says; the second reading's 'D' at position 3 comes from reading the silkscreen '- + D' in reverse pin order, and the physical D pad still carries the signal.
